comment: Ordered rebrand rules applied by rebrand.mjs to every tracked text file of a pristine DataDog/dd-sdk-reactnative tree (base: UPSTREAM_BASE = 3.5.3). Order matters: more specific rules must precede rules that match a substring of them. 'literal' rules are plain string replacement; 'regex' rules are applied with the 'g' flag and may reference capture groups in 'to' ($1). JS and native (Kotlin/Swift/ObjC) files are rebranded together so the native-module bridge names stay consistent (e.g. NativeModules.DdRum <-> @ReactModule(name="DdRum") both become Oo). Fork-owned identity files (LICENSE, NOTICE, README, .github, patches, scripts/openobserve, example) are handled by the keep-ours overlay, not here. IMPORTANT: native artifact COORDINATES (com.datadoghq:*, Datadog* pods) are NOT in 'rules' — see 'deferredRules' below; renaming them before the OpenObserve native forks are published breaks the build.

rules.why: SHIPPED + PUBLIC: consumers apply this by path — `apply from: ".../node_modules/@openobserve/mobile-react-native/datadog-sourcemaps.gradle"`. A datadog-* filename in the path a user pastes into their own build.gradle is the most visible leak there is. Specific literal, never a broad `datadog-` rule, which would rewrite the EXTERNAL datadog-ci CLI.

Specific literal, never a broad `datadog-` rule, which would rewrite the EXTERNAL datadog-ci CLI.

Dotted Java package references AND the literal directory named `com.datadog.reactnative.sessionreplay` (rn69/rnlegacy source sets use a dotted dir, not nested folders), which the com/datadog slash rule cannot match. Must precede the broad Datadog rule so the lowercase form is handled explicitly.
repository URLs in package.json / docs

The bare upstream repo/package slug — the monorepo root package name (private, ships nowhere) plus docs, CI and scripts. MUST come after the DataDog/dd-sdk-reactnative URL rule, or that rule's input is destroyed and you get the nonsense `DataDog/openobserve-react-native-rum`. NOTICE keeps the upstream name deliberately and is excluded via keep-ours.

SHIPPED: the `bin` name declared by @openobserve/mobile-react-native-babel-plugin, a PUBLISHED package. Consumers installing it get a `datadog-generate-sr-assets` executable on PATH. Lowercase, so no other rule matches it.

GUARD part 1 of 2. datadog-ci is an EXTERNAL npm package published by the upstream vendor (@datadog/datadog-ci -> 200; @openobserve/datadog-ci has never existed -> 404). An IDENTITY mapping does not protect it: rebrand.mjs applies rules SEQUENTIALLY per line, so the later '@datadog/' rule fires anyway and `yarn install` dies with a 404. Swap it to a sentinel here, restore it after the broad rule has run. Same class as the Gradle-plugin and swift-testing over-renames (doc 08 3.4).
npm scope for every workspace package (@datadog/mobile-react-native, -react-navigation, -react-native-session-replay, etc.) in one uniform rule

all camelCase Dd-prefixed identifiers -> Oo: classes, native module names, view manager names (DdRum->OoRum, DdSdkReactNative->OoSdkReactNative, DdPrivacyView->OoPrivacyView). Word-boundary guarded so it never matches mid-identifier (e.g. myDdRum). Applied to JS + native together to keep the bridge consistent.
RUM/telemetry event internal namespace field renamed _dd -> _oo (matches the rum-events-format schema fork).

Catch-all for the product/class names: Core, Internal, RUM, Logs, Trace, Flags, CrashReporting, SessionReplay, WebViewTracking, SDKReactNative. Replaces the narrow deferredRules alternation, which listed only 7 of them and silently missed DatadogTrace (28 refs), DatadogFlags (25) and DatadogSDKReactNative (100). Case-sensitive: does NOT match the `DataDog` GitHub org or lowercase `datadog-*` names, so external coordinates are untouched. Attribution lines are protected separately by ATTRIBUTION_RE in rebrand.mjs.
ACTIVATED at STEP 4 (alpha2 natives are published). Android native core Maven coordinates (-core, -rum, -logs, -okhttp, -ndk, -session-replay)

RE-PIN (STEP 4): the coordinate rule renames com.datadoghq:dd-sdk-android-* -> ai.openobserve:oo-sdk-android-* but leaves UPSTREAM's version, and ai.openobserve:oo-sdk-android-rum:3.10.0 does not exist (we publish 0.1.0-alpha2). Matches ANY version deliberately: pinning upstream's exact 3.10.0 would silently stop matching the day upstream bumps, leaving a coordinate that resolves to nothing. Update the target when the natives are re-released.

RE-PIN (STEP 4): same for the CocoaPods deps — the Datadog* -> OpenObserve* rule leaves upstream's 3.11.0, but we publish 0.1.0-alpha.2 (note the dot before the number; the Android format has none). Matches any version for the same reason.

LIVE WIRE HEADER: XHRProxy sets this on every intercepted request to stop the native layer double-counting. Verified read by NOTHING — not the iOS SDK, not the Android SDK, not the OpenObserve backend — so renaming is safe. The GraphQL headers next to it are deliberately NOT renamed: their values are already _oo-custom-header-* and the natives read exactly that.

W3C TRACESTATE vendor key. Wire-visible on EVERY traced request, and on the DEFAULT path since tracecontext became the default propagator — so removing the proprietary propagator swapped one upstream identifier on the wire for another. Invisible to every other rule (bare lowercase, no word boundary), which is the same blind spot that shipped the NTP hosts. All three SDKs had to move together or trace linking breaks between them; the backend stores trace_state opaquely and does not parse the key, so nothing server-side is affected.

deferredRules.comment: EMPTY — activated in STEP 4 once ai.openobserve:oo-sdk-android-* 0.1.0-alpha2 and the OpenObserve* pods 0.1.0-alpha.2 were live on Maven Central / CocoaPods trunk. Kept as a key so the mechanism (and the reason it existed) stays discoverable: before the native forks were published, renaming the coordinates would have broken `pod install` and Gradle resolution.

items: ddsource / ddtags query params and tags — wire protocol to the intake; handled by the backend (doc 02), not renamed client-side to avoid breaking ingest.
DD-API-KEY header — auth rename to oo-api-key is coupled to the doc 02 header-auth backend change (design §6); the native core emits it, so it is a native-fork concern, not a JS rename.
Cosmetic 'Datadog' mentions in prose/comments/links to docs.datadoghq.com — not identity-critical; handled in a later docs pass.

pathRenames.why: The Android bridge's Java package: packages/core/android/src/main/kotlin/com/datadog/reactnative/** (184 files). It SHIPS inside the published npm tarball, so the directory name reaches every consumer even though the file CONTENT was rebranded. RN's codemod had no path-rename phase at all — Android and iOS have had one since day one — so these survived every run. Content rules cannot express a rename; only `git mv` can.

fileRenames.why: PRE-EXISTING BREAKAGE, not introduced by STEP 4: the content rule \bDd([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*) -> Oo$1 renamed every IMPORT to Oo* while 103 FILES stayed Dd*, so `import { OoSdkReactNative } from './OoSdkReactNative'` pointed at DdSdkReactNative.tsx. The fork has not type-checked since the original rebrand. Anchored ^Dd(?=[A-Z]) to mirror the content rule's word boundary EXACTLY: it moves DdLogs.ts but never NativeDdFlags.ts, whose content legitimately keeps NativeDd (no boundary before Dd there). A plain substring rename would move those too and swap one broken state for another.

Class-name FILES whose basename still carries the upstream token although the class inside was rebranded (DatadogSDKWrapper.kt -> OpenObserveSDKWrapper.kt), plus the bridge podspecs (DatadogSDKReactNative.podspec). Those podspecs are NOT published to trunk (404) — they are resolved by :path via autolinking from node_modules — so renaming them is safe as long as the Podfile references move with them, which the broad content rule below handles.
Renames datadog-configuration.gradle / .schema.json / .json alongside the content rule above.
Renames datadog-sourcemaps.gradle / .schema.json / .json alongside the content rule above.

dirRenames.why: The rn69/rnlegacy source sets use a DOTTED directory name (com.datadog.reactnative.sessionreplay) rather than nested folders, so neither the com/datadog slash rule nor the `Datadog` token rule can see it. Ships inside @openobserve/mobile-react-native-session-replay.

DIRECTORIES whose basename carries the token at any depth — src/sdk/DatadogProvider, DatadogRumResource, DatadogEventEmitter, DatadogInternalBridge, and the packages/*/ios/*.xcodeproj bundles. pathRenames only matches the fixed slash-path com/datadog and cannot see these. They SHIP in the npm tarball, and the earlier pass renamed the FILES inside while stranding the directory (DatadogEventEmitter/OpenObserveEventEmitter.tsx). The .xcodeproj bundles are dev-only and referenced only by :path from the example Podfiles, which the content rules rewrite in the same run.
